text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
- Kazuyoshi Funaki of Japan won the World Cup ski jumping event at Holmenkollen on front of 55,000 enthusiastic spectators.
-Life has become harder for Norwegian judges, who are being threatened and insulted by criminals more often today than a few years ago.
-The Norwegian oil industry wants to expand internationally. The goal is to increase turnover abroad from 17.5 billion crowns in 1995 to 25 billions in 2000 and 50 billion in 2005.
-Norwegian companies lack computer expertise. Out of 350 students who graduate from computer studies every year, as many as 200 are recruited by state-owned telecommunication company Telenor.
-Heavy snowfall in the last weeks have secured water reservoir supply, which means there is now no longer any danger of a lack of electricity.
